side_a: CC 4.2.3 name the three holders' hybrid keys (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65), one per person
side_b: CC 4.5.1 a holder's primary and backup keys are one holder, under whichever of their keys is live
note: CC 4.2.3 seats one key per holder; CC 4.5.1 counts a holder under a primary or a backup key. No section says how a backup key is seated, pinned in the bundle or recognised by a verifier, and CC 4.2.6 gives recovery by a pre-committed rotation, never a standing second key. A halt or a sign-off signed by a backup key is honoured under 4.5.1 and refused under 4.2.3.

side_a: CC 5.2 "the listing, the holding claims and, by asking a member's node, the content; never the roster"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.1 "opt OUT of the mandatory DEK cascade and are Commons-tier (plaintext, holding claims at federation scope, no DEK)"
note: CC 5.2's table gives a public room's rows the audience 'the claimed nodes of the roster's members', and a node holds a row only when in its audience; CC 4.4.3.2.1 and 5.4.2 call the room Commons-tier, whose audience in the same table is every node. Whether a non-member node may hold and re-serve a public room's content differs. Beside C254 (discoverability), which is not this.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2 "the bootstrap kinds, the allegiance facts and the pairing plane are all a not-yet-Rooted sealed link carries"
side_b: CC 5.3.4 "and every row a bounded cohort delivers to that peer as its member under"
note: CC 5.3.4 lists four things that cross before Rooted (adding rows addressed to the peer and every bounded-cohort row delivered to it as a member); CC 3.3.6.2 says three are all the link carries. A reader of 3.3.6.2 alone holds family and community rows back from a member's not-yet-Rooted node. CC 5.3.4 is the home and the fuller list.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.4 The perceptual-hash tripwire likewise fires at every scope-widening promotion
side_b: CC 4.5.7 Detection runs **only at the publish/share seam of enabled groups**
note: CC 1.13.3.4 and 3.1.3.4 make the tripwire unconditional at every widening; CC 4.5.7 makes the matcher an opt-in the group's moderate-holder enables per group, on a hash list the operator provisions, and CC 4.5.13 repeats "only at enabled groups' publish/share seam". A promotion into a group that has not enabled a list is hash-matched under the first and not under the second. Neither says whether the CSAM list is the always-on case.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: execute as the same tombstone row — plane, target digest, the authorising `takedown_notice`'s id; never content
side_b: CC 7.5.5: a person's deletion inside the sealed record is the same tombstone by digest on the record's plane, citing the subject's own withdrawal or the order, written by whoever holds custody.
note: The one tombstone row carries an authorising takedown_notice id and CC 2.4.1.1's door refuses a tombstone without the notice (purge_unauthorised); CC 7.5.5 (and CC 4.5.3's own erasure paragraph: 'the ordinary tombstone by digest per plane') has a tombstone authorised by a subject's withdrawal with no notice. One implementer refuses the erasure tombstone, the other writes it.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.2: if now > deadline and completion is None:
side_b: CC 3.3.1: Breach is therefore: the window passed **and** the row is still present with none of the three composers against it.
note: The watcher of CC 4.4.3.5.2 raises the breach when the producer has emitted no consent:deletion_complete, so the emission alone clears it; CC 3.3.1 D1 says the emission never substitutes and the test is the row's presence. A producer that emits deletion_complete and keeps the row breaches under one and not the other. CC 3.3.1 also says the watcher is cancelled only by withdraws, supersedes or hard deletion; D1 is marked normative.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: authorised by a cosigned `takedown_notice` under the trust root's `consensus_protocol` with basis `steward_purge`
side_b: manifests/transitions.json takedown_notice:{basis}: one attest transition for every basis, role takedown, policy selfAct (one voice); no cosigned policy for the steward_purge leaf and no steward_purge row in governance_policy.tsv
note: The text makes a steward_purge notice a row cosigned by the trust root's seats under its protocol; the transition data admits every takedown_notice basis on one signature by a takedown duty-holder. A kernel executing the data admits a one-signer purge notice that the text's door refuses.

side_a: CC 4.2.1.1 The latch is idempotent, so a replayed or second row changes nothing.
side_b: CC 4.2.1.3 A resumption authorizes ending a *single named* `constitutional` halt, not resumption-in-general.
note: Two holders fire two halts (two ids) for one emergency. Under 4.2.1.1 the second row changes nothing: one latch, the first id, the first fuse. Under 4.2.1.3 and the confirmation rule ("names the halt by id") each halt is its own object. If the majority confirms the second id, a single-latch node sees a confirmation of a halt it never latched and lapses at the first fuse; a per-halt node stays paused. Likewise a resumption of the first id frees a single-latch node and leaves a per-halt node paused under the second. Neither section says which halt is "the currently-active" one when two have arrived.

side_a: CC 7.3.3 "any system assessed at **RM ≥ 4** opens the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation. That is the one trigger"
side_b: CC 8.8.3 "A system must pass a CRE before deployment if it meets any of:"
note: CC 7.3.3 (three times) makes RM ≥ 4 the one trigger of the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation and Annex D only the criteria it applies; Annex D-1 is headed 'Trigger criteria' and requires the evaluation on compute above 10^26 FLOP, transactional authority above $10M a day, or a recursive event, with no mention of RM. A low-RM system that meets D-1, or an RM 4 system that meets none of it, is evaluated under one and not the other.

side_a: CC 3.4.13: So a person with no assurance on record uses their own and their family's scopes freely
side_b: CC 3.2: **No minor `user` identity operates without a live adult steward.**
note: A person with no age assurance reads as under 13 (the fail-secure rule), hence a minor. CC 3.2 and CC 3.4.13 Q4 ('A guardian-less minor goes dark for general operation') stop a minor with no guardian from operating; the fail-secure paragraph lets the same person use self and family scope freely with no guardian. One build blocks every unassured new user, the other does not. The fail-secure paragraph is the newer ruling (C001) and reads the guardian rule as binding an attested minor.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: "A substrate observing emission on a family with no registry row (provisional or ratified) MUST surface it as a conformance failure (`namespace_family_unregistered`), never admit-and-wait."
side_b: CC 3.1.7: "An unregistered family has no owning component, no polarity and no reserved rule, so a consumer resolving its authority falls through to the producer-steward default."
note: What a node does with a row on a family that has no registry row. R2 says it never admits under a defaulted authority; R1 says its authority resolves to the producer-steward default, and "Where the fallback remains" keeps that default for an open-vocabulary space it does not define (an unrowed family, or the open leaves of a registered one). R1 also calls an ungated family described only in CC 3.3 conformant though unregistered. The row is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. The closed-stem passages support refusal.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7: "the fingerprint the first ten lowercase base32 characters of sha256(ed25519 public key)"
side_b: CC 2.6.8: "SHOULD raise the fingerprint length (16 characters, 80 bits, moves the bound to 2⁴⁰)"
note: The format is stated as ten characters, normative, in CC 2.6.8 and in the signed-object table; the same paragraph of CC 2.6.8 tells a large deployment to use sixteen. A verifier that recomputes ten characters refuses a sixteen-character id. Nothing says how a reader learns which length a label uses.

side_a: CC 3.2 "a strict majority of the live roster, the proposer included, or the lone path after its window with no objection"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3 "elapses and no strict majority of the *other* members objects"
note: CC 3.2 and CC 4.5.12.2 let the lone path land only with no objection; CC 3.3.6.3 lets it land unless a strict majority of the other keys object. With three keys and one objecting, a new key is admitted (or a key evicted) under 3.3.6.3 and not under 3.2. The policy rows self_roster_add and self_roster_evict (cancel: 'more than 1/2 of the others') support CC 3.3.6.3.

side_a: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "resolved through manifests/namespace_registry.json on all five row types"
note: CC 2.1 leaves the dimension unparsed by the substrate; CC 2.6.1.7, CC 2.4 (the dimension gate) and CC 3.1.7 (namespace_family_unregistered, score_outside_declared_polarity) have the admitting substrate resolve it against the registry and refuse. A row on an unregistered family is admitted under one and refused under the other. The rest of the document supports the gate.

side_a: CC 2.1: "A row naming a key outside its audience is refused `subject_outside_audience`."
side_b: data family_default_row.json: "in_audience": "no"
note: The default subject_rule of every family (157 of 184 cells, source code-v61) reads in_audience "no" and the default replication audience is cohort_plus_subjects: the shipped store admits a targeted row naming an outsider and serves it to them. The text (CC 2.1, CC 5.2) refuses the row. No departure reason or conflict row records the difference.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 "it does not un-say the prior record, it ends its liveness"
side_b: CC 3.5.1 "carries the prior's `asserted_at` and is a placement, never a competing successor"
note: A supersedes ends the prior row's liveness (CC 2.4.1 'replaces', CC 3.4.5.1); a widening is a supersedes (CC 4.4.3.3.1) yet is a placement that leaves the narrower row standing (CC 3.5.1, CC 5.2 boundary case, CC 3.2). A reader of CC 4.4.3.3.1 alone retires the narrower row on widening; whether the owner's self copy stays live and whether un-widening is possible differ. C132 and C133 are two instances of this at the owner-binding.

side_a: CC 5.4.3: "Chat and files ride a shaped link only when one end of it is shaped-only."
side_b: CC 5.4.3: "A shaped link carries rows: statements, posts, messages, reactions, the small images that fit the budget, and the control traffic of the planes."
note: Between two offering nodes that hold a shaped link, one paragraph sends chat over the unshaped link beside it and the other (with item 4, "ordinary rows are shaped") puts messages on the shaped link. Whether a message between two servers is covered differs. The carriage paragraph is the more specific.

side_a: CC 3.2: "Consumers pin `community_key_id: ciris-canonical` and resolve the live member set via `resolve_community`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "That names the founders of `ciris-canonical`, who are the three accord holders `A1`, `B1`, `C1`"
note: Whose signatures the shipped default pin trusts: CC 3.2 (and CC 5.3.4) resolve the live member set, which by CC 3.2 includes serve nodes seated as role member; CC 4.4.3.8 says the pin names the founders and never a serving install's key. The same paragraph also writes the pin as a policy value where CC 4.4.3.8 says the set is the reader's own acceptance edges and nothing else. CC 3.2 "Infrastructure does not vote" supports the founders reading.

side_a: CC 3.4.11 are the only shapes this Part registers
side_b: CC 3.4.11 provider/government rungs MAY further qualify `{level}` with a `{verifier_key}` / `{credential_class}`
note: Same sentence. The registry and the match vectors carry only age_assurance:{level}:{band}:{version}; age_assurance: is a reserved stem, so CC 3.1.7 refuses an unclaimed leaf under it as namespace_family_unregistered. A producer using the MAY emits a row every conformant substrate refuses. The registry supports "only two shapes".

side_a: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
side_b: manifests/transitions.json (ownership:{relation}:{target_kind}:{version}, withdraw): "when(verb=withdraw,has=wa_adjudication_ref) one wa_adjudication:{state}@admitted[id=ref:wa_adjudication_ref] else refuse"
note: The data puts the recovery guard on the ownership:* mirror row and fires it only when the reference is present; the owner-binding itself (self:delegates_to) has one transition, authorize, and no withdraw, supersede or lapse. The text's gate (a subject or delegate withdrawal with no reference is refused) and the owner's own withdrawal are not in the data.
